name: Population genomics
title: Why deCODE went bankrupt, and when genomics got cheap enough
question: Why did deCODE genetics go bankrupt, and when did genome sequencing get cheap enough?
answer: deCODE (1996) set out to read the genetics of a nation, Iceland. It filed for Chapter 11 in 2009 and Amgen bought it in 2012 for $415M. NHGRI measured the cost of sequencing a genome at about $95M in 2001, about $70,000 in 2009 and a few hundred dollars by 2022. 23andMe (2006) built a consumer business on the same curve, then filed for bankruptcy itself in 2025.
verdict_reason: Sequencing cost collapsed after 2008; population genomics became routine.

constraint.name: Cost of reading DNA
constraint.detail: At millions of dollars per genome, population-scale genetics could not pay back.

crossing.text: Next-generation sequencing cuts NHGRI's cost per genome from $7.1M (2007) to $342,500 (2008).
